oil.summary: Crude markets are caught in a tug-of-war between supply recovery and geopolitical risk. WTI slipped 0.65% to $85.48/bbl while Brent barely held positive at $91.63, masking a brutal month that has seen Brent shed over 13%. The key supply-side development: Saudi Arabia reported a 26% jump in October output to 10.563 mb/d, near pre-war levels, and OPEC broadly confirms production is normalising in the Strait of Hormuz corridor — crude export flows back to 80-85% of pre-war capacity. Options markets price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the May meeting, flagging bearish medium-term sentiment. Offsetting the supply surge, Iran's denial of any US negotiations briefly spiked Brent nearly 3% intraday. Ukrainian drones reportedly cut Russian refining capacity by 30%, consistent with the sharp 2.45% drop in RBOB gasoline and the relative outperformance of heating oil (+1.20%), where Russian diesel disruption and UK sanctions on 22 Russian tankers tighten distillate balances.
drivers: Saudi Arabia output surged 26% in October to 10.563 mb/d, reinforcing supply recovery and weighing on flat-price crude
Ukraine drone strikes cut Russian refining capacity by an estimated 30%, tightening distillate markets and lifting heating oil even as RBOB sold off sharply
Iran war risk premium volatile — Iran's denial of US talks triggered an intraday Brent spike of nearly 3%, but US downplaying of further strikes kept net gains capped

gas.summary: Natural gas markets diverged sharply across geographies. Henry Hub pulled back 0.64% to $3.275/MMBtu on the day but remains up over 10% on the week, suggesting recent strength is consolidating rather than reversing. European TTF gained 2.94% to €87.22/MWh, bouncing from a one-month low hit Tuesday as Iran war uncertainty re-entered the market — Tehran's warning of domestic gas shortages caused by the conflict added a fresh supply-risk narrative. Germany's decision to award all 5.16 GW of its inaugural capacity auction to gas-fired projects underscores how critical gas remains for European power security, structurally underpinning TTF. UK sanctions on 22 Russian tankers add further tail risk to European LNG and pipeline balances. Pro-Palestinian activists are now targeting Murphy Oil over Israeli offshore gas licenses, though near-term market impact appears limited.
drivers: TTF rebounded 2.94% as Iran war uncertainty returned; Tehran warned of domestic gas shortages, reinforcing regional supply risk
Germany awarded all 5.16 GW of its first capacity auction to gas-fired generation, cementing structural European gas demand
UK sanctions on 22 Russian tankers tighten potential LNG and pipeline supply routes into Europe, adding upside tail risk to TTF

power.summary: EU carbon edged up 0.56% to $83.88/EUA, holding a marginal positive on the month despite a week-to-date decline of over 2%, with TTF's 2.94% daily rise providing supportive cost-push pressure. The macro backdrop at COP31 is constructive for long-term grid investment — IRENA reported over 21,000 km of new transmission lines built last year, a 50% surge to a record high. Germany's gas-capacity auction result highlights the tension between near-term security of supply and net-zero targets, an issue also confronting Andy Burnham at COP31. Russia launched 128 attacks on Ukraine's energy grid in a single week, underscoring infrastructure vulnerability. Longer-dated themes in focus include quantum computing pitched as a solution to AI's growing power demand, and a record year for private investment in fusion superconducting technology — both too early-stage to affect current EUA pricing but shaping the demand outlook.
drivers: TTF's 2.94% daily gain provides cost-push support to EUA as carbon and gas prices remain correlated through gas-fired power generation
IRENA reported a 50% surge in global grid expansion to over 21,000 km of new transmission lines, highlighted at COP31, reinforcing long-term electrification investment thesis
Russia's 128 weekly attacks on Ukraine's energy grid and ongoing Iran war uncertainty keep European power security in focus, supporting capacity and carbon premiums
